primitives.name: Scoring Function Evaluation Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: In general, one aspect of the subject matter described in this specification can be embodied in a method that includes the acts of receiving a first query and selecting a first and a second candidate scoring function from a plurality of candidate scoring functions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q': 'search query (dimensionless)', 'S_1, S_2': 'candidate scoring functions (dimensionless)', 'R_1, R_2': 'ranked search results (ordered set)'}
primitives.assumptions: Search queries are static; scoring functions map documents to relevance scores; ranking is deterministic per function.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_1 and S_2 produce identical rankings for all Q, evaluation becomes inconclusive.

layer2.mapping: Pairwise ranking comparison mirrors Bayesian hypothesis testing over relevance models.
layer2.telemetry: User preference alignment between ranked result sets

primitives.name: Ranked Result Pairwise Comparison
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method further includes presenting the plurality of first search results ordered according to scores from the first scoring function; and presenting the plurality of first search results ordered according to scores from the second scoring function.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{S_1}, R_{S_2}': 'ranked results under S_1 and S_2 (ordered sequences)', 'P(R_{S_1}, R_{S_2})': 'probability of ranking agreement (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rankings are complete and consistent; user preference is transitive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When both rankings are identical, P(R_{S_1}, R_{S_2}) = 1; when completely inverted, P = 0.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of pairwise rank discrepancy used in GSE state transition logic.

primitives.name: User Preference Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: First input selecting the first scoring function over the second scoring function can be received, and an order for the plurality of scoring functions can be generated based on the first input.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'U': 'user preference signal (dimensionless)', 'S_i \\in \\mathcal{S}': 'scoring function (dimensionless)', '\\mathcal{S}': 'set of scoring functions (finite set)'}
primitives.assumptions: User preferences are binary and transitive; input reflects true preference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If U is absent or ambiguous, no ordering can be inferred.

layer2.mapping: User preference induces a partial order on scoring functions, aligning with GSI's Bayesian ranking.
layer2.telemetry: Preference consistency across multiple query sessions

reasoning_traces.think:
The framework evaluates web search scoring functions by comparing their outputs on identical queries. Each scoring function assigns a relevance score to documents, which are then ranked. The core operator is the pairwise comparison of these rankings, modeled as a stochastic process where user preference determines outcome likelihood. The system assumes that differences in ranking reflect differences in scoring function efficacy. A key duality exists: the evaluation process is symmetric in that any two functions can be compared, yet the full ordering requires transitivity. Failure modes arise when functions yield identical rankings or when user feedback is inconsistent or absent. The framework enables a Bayesian approach to ranking, where posterior probabilities over function quality are updated based on observed preferences. This supports GSE’s dynamic reasoning over evolving search landscapes, while GSI uses the same structure for conformal prediction of relevance confidence intervals.
